newsitem.title: USA: Dow edges lower as tobacco shares weaken.
newsitem.headline: Dow edges lower as tobacco shares weaken.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks edged lower Friday as investors sold off tobacco shares and several top-name firms that reported disappointing profits.
Tobacco stocks came under renewed selling pressure in the wake of new evidence directly linking smoking to lung cancer.

Just after 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was down 0.75 point to 6,058.45, dragged lower by component stock Philip Morris Cos. Inc. The food and tobacco company's stock tumbled 4-7/8 to 92-1/2.
On the broader market, advancing issues slightly outpaced decliners on New York Stock Exchange volume of 274 million shares.

"The story of the tobacco stocks is that it is inevitable that some day the companies will have to pay some great amount of money to somebody," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd.
Tobacco shares were weak across the board, with RJR Nabisco Holdings off 1-5/8 to 25-7/8 and Loews Corp. down 2-3/8 to 79-1/4.
Faring even worse was Xerox Corp., which stunned Wall Street with third-quarter earnings far short of expectations.
Xerox, the NYSE's most active issue, plummeted 9-3/4 to 47-1/4 as investors bailed out of the stock. Prudential Securities removed Xerox from its "Best Idea" list following release of its earnings.
The sharp fall "points to the worries about 1997 earnings and dramatises how deep those worries are," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.

McDonald's Corp. fell 1 to 45-1/2 after the company reported slightly lower-than-expected third-quarter earnings. The compay said its U.S. operating performance was not keeping pace with its goals and third-quarter operating income had fallen from last year.
Oil companies remained firm, with Texaco Inc. up 1 at 103 and Exxon Corp. up 7/8 at 89.
Nasdaq stocks continued to be buffeted by a wave of selling that began after the Nasdaq Composite index reached record highs Monday and Tuesday.

"Stocks that had been big performers are seeing some serious profit-taking," said Bleier. He cited modem maker U.S. Robotics Inc., which fell 2 to 74, and Intel Corp., which dipped 1-1/4 to 109-1/2, as examples.
Microsoft Corp. also extended its retreat from recent highs, down 1-3/16 to 134-5/16. SoundView Financial downgraded the shares Friday morning to hold from buy.
The Nasdaq Composite index was down 2.49 points at 1,239.47, and the American Stock Exchange index lost 0.03 at 577.36.
